items.title: 日銀總裁的「鷹派立場」未讓市場理解及接受 日元跌勢加劇
items.title_en: Bank of Japan Governor's Hawkish Stance Not Understood or Accepted by Market, Yen Decline Accelerates
paras: 日本央行總裁植田和男周五(18日)在記者會上，傳達出對於升息更為積極的鷹派姿態，然而日元不僅未能止跌，跌勢反倒進一步擴大。分析師指出，主因是植田的說法未讓投資者理解及滿意。
日本外匯市場周五傍晚，日元兌美元匯率一度跌至157區間後段，較紐約市場收盤時的跌幅達1.2%。日本央行在貨幣政策會議上將政策利率從之前的1%上調至1.25%，植田則重申繼續升息立場。

短期承壓：政策訊息混淆

Reed Capital 投資總監 Gerald Gan 表示，儘管植田試圖平息市場情緒，但他仍維持短期內日元將持續疲軟的看法，並強調日銀與美國聯準會(Fed)在前瞻指引上的分歧，正成為影響日元穩定的主要疑慮。
富國銀行(Wells Fargo)亞太區策略負責人 Chidu Narayana 指出，植田的鷹派態度不足以支持市場原本過於激進的期待，在缺乏明確鷹派信號與美元反彈下，美元兌日元匯率將維持高位。
Stonex Financial 利率主管 Shriya Samarth 認為，日銀傳遞的訊息相當混淆，既承認政策優先順序改變，又不願承諾面對通膨上行風險，難以被市場認定為足夠鷹派。T&D 資產管理首席策略師Hiroshi Namioka補充，市場難解讀植田的發言，導致日元短暫走強後再度重回貶勢。

結構性壓力與市場干預風險

Pictet Asset Management Japan 投資策略部長田中純平分析，植田宣示「政策營運階段改變」，雖有助於消除市場對日銀落後於曲線的疑慮，但受制於日元面臨的結構性下行壓力，加上市場預期的日美升息步調差異有限，僅憑本次會議結果難以觸發持續性的日元升值行情。
此外，他提醒連休期間交易清淡，投資人仍需戒備日美政府進行協調干預的可能性，預期美元兌日元將持續劇烈波動且缺乏明確方向。

部分分析師看好日元中長期走升

不過，部分分析師持較為樂觀的態度。SMBC 信託銀行投資調查部長山口真弘認為，植田成功化解了記者會可能引發日元急跌的風險，且日銀的基本立場並未改變，市場仍維持每3個月升息一次(如今年 12 月)的預期，因此不認為日元會陷入長期走貶趨勢。
State Street Investment Management 資深固定收益策略師Masahiko Loo強調，市場不應過度解讀兩位審議委員的反對票，美元兌日元在 160 附近仍宜採取逢高賣出策略。他預測，隨著日銀政策正常化帶動國內殖利率上升、日本資產吸引機構資金回流，以及 AI 相關投資增加等三大結構性因素，日元中長期走勢將逐漸獲得支撐。
paras_en: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday (the 18th) conveyed a more aggressive hawkish stance toward rate hikes at a press conference, yet the yen not only failed to stop falling, its decline actually widened. Analysts said the main reason was that Ueda's remarks did not resonate with or satisfy investors.

In the Japanese foreign‑exchange market on Friday evening, the yen slipped to the lower end of the 157 range against the dollar, a 1.2% drop from the New York close. The BOJ raised its policy rate from 1.0% to 1.25% at its monetary‑policy meeting, and Ueda reiterated the commitment to continue raising rates.

Short‑term pressure: mixed policy signals
Gerald Gan, Investment Director at Reed Capital, said that despite Ueda’s attempt to calm market sentiment, he still expects the yen to remain weak in the short run and highlighted the growing divergence between the BOJ and the U.S. Federal Reserve on forward guidance as a key concern for yen stability.

Chidu Narayana, Head of Asia‑Pacific Strategy at Wells Fargo, noted that Ueda’s hawkish tone was insufficient to meet the market’s overly aggressive expectations, and without a clear hawkish signal and a dollar rebound, the dollar‑yen pair is likely to stay elevated.

Shriya Samarth, Head of Rates at Stonex Financial, said the BOJ’s messaging was quite confusing – it acknowledged a shift in policy priorities but was unwilling to commit to tackling upside inflation risks, making it hard for the market to view the stance as sufficiently hawkish. Hiroshi Namioka, Chief Strategist at T&D Asset Management, added that the market struggled to interpret Ueda’s comments, causing a brief yen rally that quickly reverted to depreciation.

Structural pressure and intervention risk
Junpei Tanaka, Head of Investment Strategy for Japan at Pictet Asset Management, analyzed that Ueda’s declaration of a “change in the policy operating phase” helps allay concerns that the BOJ is lagging behind the yield curve, but the yen faces structural downward pressure and the expected gap between Japan and U.S. rate‑hiking paths is limited, so the meeting outcome alone is unlikely to trigger a sustained yen appreciation rally.

He also warned that trading is thin over the holiday period and investors should remain vigilant about the possibility of coordinated intervention by Japanese and U.S. authorities, expecting the dollar‑yen to continue swinging wildly with no clear direction.

Some analysts are bullish on the yen over the medium to long term
Nevertheless, a few analysts are more optimistic. Masahiro Yamaguchi, Head of Investment Research at SMBC Trust Bank, believes Ueda successfully defused the risk of a sharp yen drop that could have arisen from the press conference, and that the BOJ’s fundamental stance remains unchanged. The market still expects a rate hike every three months (e.g., in December), so he does not see the yen entering a long‑term downtrend.

Masahiko Loo, Senior Fixed‑Income Strategist at State Street Investment Management, stressed that the market should not over‑interpret the dissenting votes of two board members. He recommends selling on rallies near the 160 level for the dollar‑yen. He forecasts that as BOJ policy normalises, domestic yields rise, Japanese assets attract institutional inflows, and AI‑related investments grow, three structural factors will gradually support the yen’s medium‑ to long‑term trajectory.

items.title: 升息過後為何日元摔、日股漲？解析日銀決策被解讀不夠鷹派的三大關鍵
items.title_en: Why Did the Yen Fall and the Nikkei Rise After the Rate Hike? Three Key Factors Behind the BOJ's Less Hawkish Decision
paras: 日本銀行(央行，BOJ)周五(18日)將升息1碼(25個基點)至1.25%，利率創1995年以來最高，且升息間隔從之前的六個月縮短為三個月。儘管升息步調加快，日本金融市場卻出現違反直覺的走勢：日元走弱、10年期日本公債殖利率下滑，日經225指數上漲。
分析師指出，日銀理事會表決出現兩張反對升息票，加上本次升息並未同步公布最新經濟展望，都讓市場解讀日銀不夠鷹派。
目前市場預期，日銀可能在12月左右再次升息，但對利率最終將升至多高卻看法不一。
升息通常會帶動一國貨幣上揚、推升債券殖利率，並對股市造成壓力，但日本的貨幣、債券殖利率與股市周五卻出現完全相反的走勢。截稿前，日元跌破157日元兌1美元，10年期日本政府公債殖利率下滑，日經225指數收盤上漲1.4%。

升息決策7票對2票 市場解讀不夠鷹派

專家指出，日銀理事會出現分歧，是市場出現非典型反應的原因，因為這顯示日本央行可能不會採取過於鷹派的立場。
日本銀行三井住友銀行(SMBC)首席外匯策略師Hirofumi Suzuki說：「兩票反對升息、主張維持利率不變，令人感到意外。」
本次升息決策以七票對兩票通過，理事淺田統一郎(Toichiro Asada)與佐藤綾野(Ayano Sato)投下反對票，他們是由首相高市早苗今年稍早任命、被視為恢復通膨派的人馬。
佐藤綾野指出，由於核心通膨率低於2%，經濟情勢可能還不夠強勁，因此主張維持利率不變。日本8月核心通膨率微降至1.7%，低於7月的1.8%。
淺田統一郎也表示，與先前相比，目前經濟與物價發展似乎沒有大幅加速。

未同步更新經濟展望

道富投資管理公司(State Street Investment Management)資深固定收益策略師Masahiko Loo指出，此次升息未同步公布更新版的經濟展望報告，也是市場反直覺回應的原因之一，因為這限制了日銀透過調整預測來強化鷹派訊息的能力。
牛津經濟學(Oxford Economics)日本經濟主管Shigeto Nagai認同這項看法，他表示，兩名反對升息的理事傳遞的訊號是，高市早苗並未確定接受美國要求日本加快升息的主張。
路透周五報導，美國財長貝森特(Scott Bessent)5月與日本財務大臣片山皋月(Satsuki Katayama)會面時，曾強調日銀需要提高利率。
Nagai進一步補充說：「其次，如果我們觀察聲明，所有措辭與語氣幾乎都與7月公布的季度展望報告相同，因此語氣不像金融市場原本期待的那麼鷹派。」

利率還能升多少？

專家目前認為，日銀可能在12月左右再次升息。
道富的Loo表示，他預期日銀總裁植田和男將強調，未來每一次政策會議都仍然「有可能升息」。他說：「如今爭論的已經不是日銀是否升息，而是利率最終會升到多高。」
日銀表示，隨著經濟與物價情勢發展，將持續調升利率。不過，日銀也承認，中東衝突推升油價，可能導致經濟成長放緩。
EFG International經濟學家Sam Jochim表示，隨著潛在通膨率接近2%，利率可能大約每三個月調升一次。他預期，2027年的終點利率、也就是利率可能達到的峰值，將落在1.75%至2%之間。
BOJ並未預測終點利率，而是持續表示將「適當」執行貨幣政策，以讓潛在通膨率穩定在約2%的目標。
穆迪分析(Moody’s Analytics)亞太區經濟主管Stefan Angrick預期，日銀可能在今年底至明年初再度升息，但需求帶動的通膨疲弱，加上實質薪資成長令人失望，將限縮後續的升息幅度。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) raised rates by one point (25 basis points) to 1.25% on Friday, the highest level since 1995, and shortened the interval between hikes from six months to three months. Despite the faster pace, Japanese financial markets behaved counterintuitively: the yen weakened, the 10‑year Japanese government bond yield fell, and the Nikkei 225 rose.

Analysts say that the BOJ board’s vote included two dissenting votes against the hike, and that the hike was announced without a new economic outlook, leading markets to view the BOJ as not sufficiently hawkish.
The market currently expects the BOJ may hike again around December, but opinions differ on how high rates will ultimately rise.

Rate hikes usually lift a currency, push bond yields higher, and pressure equity markets, yet on Friday the yen fell, the 10‑year yield dropped, and the Nikkei 225 closed up 1.4% as the yen slipped below 157 per dollar.
The 7‑to‑2 vote on the hike was seen as insufficiently hawkish by markets.
SMBC’s chief FX strategist Hirofumi Suzuki said, "The two dissenting votes and the call to keep rates unchanged were surprising."
The vote passed 7‑to‑2, with Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato casting the opposing votes. They were appointed by Prime Minister Fumio Kishida earlier this year and are seen as pro‑inflation advocates.
Sato argued that because core inflation was below 2%, the economy might not yet be strong enough, so rates should stay unchanged. Japan’s core inflation fell to 1.7% in August from 1.8% in July.
Asada also said that, compared to before, the current economic and price developments do not appear to have accelerated significantly.

The hike was announced without an updated economic outlook, which, according to State Street Investment Management’s senior fixed‑income strategist Masahiko Loo, is one reason for the counterintuitive market reaction, as it limited the BOJ’s ability to reinforce a hawkish message through revised forecasts.
Oxford Economics’ Japan chief Shigeto Nagai agreed, noting that the two dissenting board members signaled that Kishida had not yet committed to the U.S. demand for faster hikes.
Reuters reported on Friday that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a May meeting with Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama, emphasized that the BOJ needed to raise rates.
Nagai added, "Moreover, if we look at the statement, all wording and tone are almost identical to the July quarterly outlook, so the tone is not as hawkish as markets had expected."
How much higher can rates go? Experts currently think the BOJ may hike again around December.

Loo said he expects BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda to emphasize that every future policy meeting still "could involve a rate hike." He added, "The debate now is not whether the BOJ will hike, but how high rates will ultimately rise."

The BOJ said it will continue to raise rates as the economy and price conditions evolve, but it also acknowledged that the Middle East conflict has pushed oil prices up, potentially slowing economic growth.

EFG International economist Sam Jochim said that as the potential inflation rate approaches 2%, rates may rise roughly every three months. He expects the 2027 endpoint rate, the peak rate, to fall between 1.75% and 2%.
The BOJ has not forecasted an endpoint rate but continues to say it will "appropriately" conduct monetary policy to keep potential inflation around the 2% target.

Moody’s Analytics Asia‑Pacific chief economist Stefan Angrick expects the BOJ may hike again at the end of this year or early next year, but weak demand‑driven inflation and disappointing real wage growth will limit future hikes.
